answer: A voyage across an open network is safe only if travelers are real, so a sybil defense should make fake identities costly. One design is a time-locked bond: each identity locks tokens for thirty days before its votes count, and the bond is slashed if its attestations are shown to be copied. An attacker running fifty fake identities must lock fifty bonds and risk losing all. Like a plume of smoke revealing a fire, correlated answers expose clusters. As the tide of rewards rises, cheating costs more than honest work.
